subject: humanities
passage: Commedia dell'arte, a popular form of theater in sixteenth-century Italy, did not use full written scripts. Troupes worked from a short outline of the plot that was often pinned up backstage. Each actor played the same masked character for years and knew that character's jokes and habits well, so performers could ______ their lines on the spot, changing them to suit each audience.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The troupes had no "full written scripts," only a plot outline, and actors made up their lines "on the spot" to suit each audience. Making something up in the moment is improvising, so "improvise" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. With no full scripts, there were no written lines to memorize, and the lines changed "on the spot."
explanation.B: Incorrect. To transcribe is to write words down, but the text stresses that the troupes did not use written scripts and made up their lines "on the spot."
explanation.C: Correct. Actors who knew their characters well could invent, or improvise, their lines on the spot from a plot outline.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how loudly actors spoke; it is about where their words came from.
